description: Executable evidence for the SDK precheck clauses: an Event Envelope or payload that fails validation is refused before consumption and leaves no effect; the members that carry authorization cannot be omitted or defaulted and the four members that are forbidden at the Event top level are refused; an unknown critical extension and an unmet requirement each fail closed, while an unknown non-critical extension is preserved. Schema admissibility is not the observation point in any case: each case observes the absence or presence of a consumed effect.

cases.name: an_envelope_that_fails_the_event_schema_never_reaches_the_reducer
cases.given: an Event Envelope that does not satisfy ak.schema.event.v1, delivered through the ordinary ingest path
cases.action: submit it to the SDK and then read every surface the SDK exposes
cases.observed: the returned outcome, the reducer state, the local projection and every query result
assertions: the call returns schema_violation
no reducer state changed
the object does not appear in any projection, query result or local cache
schema admissibility alone is not what this case asserts: the observation point is the absence of a consumed effect

cases.name: a_payload_that_fails_its_payload_class_never_reaches_the_reducer
cases.given: an Event Envelope that satisfies ak.schema.event.v1 but whose payload does not satisfy the payload class its event kind declares
cases.action: submit it and read every exposed surface
cases.observed: the returned outcome and the reducer state
assertions: the call returns schema_violation
no reducer state changed, so envelope-level admissibility does not open a path for an inadmissible payload
the payload class is resolved from the declared event kind rather than guessed from the payload shape

cases.name: a_rejected_envelope_is_not_repaired_or_partially_applied
cases.given: an envelope rejected by the previous two cases and an SDK that owns a retry queue
cases.action: run every retry, reconnect and backfill path the SDK exposes
cases.observed: the reducer state and the outbound queue after each path runs
assertions: no path re-admits the rejected object
nothing is normalized, defaulted or repaired into an admissible form
no partial effect of the rejected object survives anywhere

cases.name: hlc_at_the_event_top_level_is_refused
cases.given: an otherwise valid Event Envelope carrying hlc as a top-level member
assertions: the member is refused rather than ignored or stripped
the refusal is schema_violation, not a softer acceptance with a warning

cases.name: producer_revision_at_the_event_top_level_is_refused
cases.given: an otherwise valid Event Envelope carrying producer_revision as a top-level member
assertions: the member is refused rather than ignored or stripped
the refusal is schema_violation

cases.name: domain_refs_at_the_event_top_level_is_refused
cases.given: an otherwise valid Event Envelope carrying domain_refs as a top-level member
assertions: the member is refused rather than ignored or stripped
the refusal is schema_violation

cases.name: requirements_at_the_event_top_level_is_refused
cases.given: an otherwise valid Event Envelope carrying requirements as a top-level member
assertions: the member is refused rather than ignored or stripped
the refusal is schema_violation
top-level requirements is refused here, which is a different observation from the unmet-requirements semantics exercised by the requirements vector

cases.name: the_authorization_carrying_members_cannot_be_omitted_or_defaulted
cases.given: four envelopes, each omitting exactly one of proofs, scope_ref, actor_id and refs with role authorized_by
cases.action: submit each and inspect what the verification path did with the missing member
cases.observed: the returned outcome for each envelope and the values the verification path used
assertions: each omission is refused on its own
no member is filled in from a default, from the transport, from the session or from a neighbouring event
the verification path is not reached with a synthesized value in place of the missing member

cases.name: an_unknown_critical_extension_fails_closed
cases.given: an object declaring a critical extension this build does not recognise, valid in every other respect
cases.observed: the returned outcome and the reducer state
assertions: the object is refused as a whole
no part of it is applied, and the unrecognised extension is not skipped so the rest can proceed
the decision is made from the criticality declaration, not from whether the extension body happens to parse

cases.name: unmet_requirements_fail_closed
cases.given: an object whose declared requirements name a capability this build does not provide, with no unknown extension present
cases.observed: the returned outcome and the reducer state
assertions: the object is refused because the requirement is unmet, which is a different decision from an unknown critical extension
no part of it is applied
a build that provides the capability admits the identical object, so the case observes the requirement check and not a schema failure

cases.name: an_unknown_non_critical_extension_is_preserved_and_admitted
cases.given: an object carrying an unknown extension that is not declared critical
cases.action: consume it, then re-encode and forward it
cases.observed: the admission outcome and the re-encoded bytes
assertions: the object is admitted
the unknown extension survives the round trip byte for byte
an implementation that refused every unknown value would fail here, which is why fail-closed is scoped to criticality and to requirements

cases.name: the_fail_closed_decision_precedes_consumption_and_storage
cases.given: the two refusing objects above and an SDK that owns a durable store
cases.action: submit each, then inspect the durable store, the projection and the outbound queue
cases.observed: the durable store, the projection and the outbound queue
assertions: neither object is stored, projected or forwarded
the refusal happens before any payload member is consumed
a later registry refresh does not resurrect the refused object from a staged copy, because no copy was staged
